one_liner: Clip-on vibration and temperature sensors with a self-learning model that sends WhatsApp alerts before small-factory motors and pumps fail.
sub_sector: Industrial IoT predictive maintenance for MSME factories
ask: INR 2.2 Cr at INR 11 Cr post-money
business_model: Hardware sale (INR 9,500 per sensor, INR 3,200 cost) plus INR 750 per sensor per month subscription at ~85% gross margin.

founders.name: Karthik Subramanian
founders.background_claimed: IIT Madras (mechanical); 5 years as a reliability engineer at an engine maker.

founders.name: Neeraj Pillai
founders.background_claimed: 4 years in embedded systems at an auto-components supplier; designed the sensor board and firmware.

claims.text: 6 of 11 pilots converted to paid (55%); 140 paid sensors live, averaging 23 per paying customer; monthly recurring subscription INR 1.05 L.
claims.note: Internally consistent: 140 x INR 750 = INR 1.05 L MRR. Paid sensors grew 20 -> 48 -> 80 -> 112 -> 140 from June to October (D6).

claims.text: Cumulative subscription revenue looks too low for the deck's sensor ramp: form gives INR 14.2 L cumulative revenue of which INR 13.3 L hardware, leaving ~INR 0.9 L non-hardware; the deck's paid-sensor chart at INR 750/sensor/month implies roughly INR 3 L of subscription billed June-October.
claims.note: Arithmetic from the founders' own figures (20+48+80+112+140 sensor-months x INR 750 = INR 3.0 L). Possible explanations: free months after pilots, annual billing, or unpaid invoices. Hardware (INR 13.3 L = 140 x 9,500) is ~94% of revenue to date.

claims.text: Business is hardware-heavy today: INR 9,500 per sensor against INR 3,200 cost, plus INR 750 per sensor per month subscription at ~85% gross margin; average customer worth ~INR 3.1 L first-year gross profit.
claims.note: Checks out: 23 x 6,300 hardware GP + 23 x 750 x 12 x 0.85 = ~INR 3.2 L. Most of it is one-off hardware margin, so 'payback' (D19) is mostly hardware-funded.

claims.text: Cost per paid customer is ~INR 73,000 (INR 4.4 L cost of 11 pilots / 6 paid customers), excluding founder time; a pilot is 10 free sensors for 30 days.
Channels: 3 of 6 paid customers via a cluster association, 2 via a pump distributor, 1 direct.
claims.note: Channel concentration: one association accounts for half of paid customers.

claims.text: Customers report 9 unplanned stoppages caught early during pilots at an estimated INR 1.8 L downtime cost each; the founders state these are customer-reported and unaudited.
claims.note: This is the closest thing to the deeptech 'live-site pilot result'. Founders flag it as unaudited themselves, which is a good sign of candour.

claims.text: Founders visited 38 plants in the Pune and Coimbatore clusters (Nov 2025-Feb 2026) before scaling pilots.
Founders name their own key risks: sensor accuracy across motor types, hardware supply, and longer sales cycles in larger plants.
claims.note: Relevant to R1 (owns the defining risk).

claims.text: 12-month targets are internally inconsistent: 30 paying customers at the current ~23 sensors each would be ~690 sensors, i.e. ~INR 5.2 L MRR at INR 750/sensor, not the INR 12 L MRR targeted (which needs ~1,600 sensors, ~53 per customer).
claims.note: Derived from the founders' own numbers; ask which assumption (sensors per customer, price, or customer count) drives the INR 12 L.

claims.text: 25% of the raise is earmarked for 'Certification and operations', but the application does not name which certifications are needed or the timeline.
claims.note: Sensors use low-power radios (D18). Wireless devices sold in India generally need WPC Equipment Type Approval (W5, framed by the source for imports); the founders should state their certification path.

claims.text: Deck claims imported condition monitors cost INR 40,000+ per motor with annual contracts.
claims.note: Pricing of imported systems not verified; no page with a citable price was retrieved.

claims.text: Pune-based Infinite Uptime, a predictive-maintenance provider for industrial machinery, raised USD 35M Series C (March 2025, led by Avataar Ventures).
claims.note: Well-funded competitor in the same city; deck positions only against 'imported systems' and manual rounds.

claims.text: Pump maker Kirloskar Brothers sells KirloSmart, an IoT pump-monitoring system that generates alerts for probable causes of pump failure.
claims.note: Incumbent pump OEM with its own monitoring product; also a possible channel/partner given Pumpwise sells through pump distributors.

claims.text: A BITS Pilani Hyderabad startup launched machine health monitoring products for MSMEs (Mach-Sevak for smaller units) in 2025.
claims.note: Evidence of other MSME-focused monitoring entrants.

claims.text: Founders: Karthik Subramanian (CEO) claims IIT Madras mechanical engineering and 5 years as a reliability engineer at an engine maker; Neeraj Pillai (CTO) claims 4 years in embedded systems at an auto-components supplier and designed the sensor and firmware. No prior startup experience; full-time since October 2025.
claims.note: Pedigree (IIT) is capped by the fund's pedigree rule; relevant domain experience is the stronger signal but unverified.

claims.text: Founder LinkedIn links are placeholders (*-example) and the website is a .example domain; no independent footprint for the founders or the company was found.
Team of 7; sensors made by a contract manufacturer in Pune.
claims.note: Single contract manufacturer = supply risk the founders themselves list (F9).

claims.text: Market sizing (TAM INR 16,200 Cr) assumes 300K MSMEs with 20+ motors, a share derived from the founders' own plant visits; subscription only.
Sector as selected is Deeptech; the business is industrial IoT hardware plus subscription analytics, which fits deeptech.
Raising INR 2.2 Cr at INR 11 Cr post-money; existing capital INR 30 L (INR 10 L incubator grant + INR 20 L from two angels).
Founders invite scrutiny of manufacturing scale-up and calibration and offer to share pilot data.

gaps.what: Karthik Subramanian (CEO): no public footprint confirming IIT Madras or the reliability-engineer role at an engine maker.
gaps.why_it_matters: Domain credibility in reliability engineering is the core founder claim.
searched: WebSearch: "Karthik Subramanian" Pumpwise Pune predictive maintenance (2026-11-18) - no match; results were Infinite Uptime, Kirloskar, others
Application LinkedIn link linkedin.com/in/karthik- subramanian-example is a placeholder
gaps.ask_founder: Which engine maker, which years, and can we see your IIT Madras degree or speak to a former manager?

gaps.what: Neeraj Pillai (CTO): no public footprint confirming embedded-systems work at an auto-components supplier.
gaps.why_it_matters: He designed the sensor and firmware; hardware execution risk sits with him.
searched: WebSearch: "Neeraj Pillai" Pumpwise embedded Pune (2026-11-18) - only an unrelated Mumbai product manager profile
Application LinkedIn link linkedin.com/in/neeraj-pillai-example is a placeholder
gaps.ask_founder: Which supplier and products did you work on; any prior hardware shipped at volume?

gaps.what: Company existence: no website, MCA record, press or customer reference found for Pumpwise Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
gaps.why_it_matters: Basic verification of entity and customers.
searched: WebSearch: Pumpwise Technologies Pune motor pump sensor (2026-11-18) - no result
gaps.ask_founder: Share CIN, and introductions to two paying customers and the cluster association.

gaps.what: Subscription revenue reconciliation: ~INR 0.9 L cumulative non-hardware revenue vs ~INR 3 L implied by the paid-sensor ramp.
gaps.why_it_matters: Recurring revenue is the deciding quality-of-revenue question for a hardware+SaaS model.
searched: Form Revenue answer vs deck slide 6 chart and slide 9 pricing
gaps.ask_founder: How much subscription has actually been invoiced and collected to date, by month, and are any customers on free months?

gaps.what: Measured model accuracy: false-alert and missed-failure rates across motor types.
gaps.why_it_matters: The founders list accuracy as their top risk; the only value evidence is 9 customer-reported catches, unaudited.
searched: Form Evidence of value and Key risks
gaps.ask_founder: Across 140 sensors, how many alerts fired, how many were confirmed faults, and were any failures missed?

gaps.what: Certification and regulatory path: which approvals (e.g. WPC ETA for the radio, any electrical/hazardous-area certifications) and timeline.
gaps.why_it_matters: A quarter of the raise is for certification; deeptech key metric is the certification path.
gaps.ask_founder: Which certifications do you need before selling to larger plants, what do they cost and when will you have them?

gaps.what: Liability if a monitored motor fails without an alert; contract terms and insurance.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deeptech key metric 'liability and insurance' is absent from the application.
gaps.ask_founder: What do your customer contracts say about missed failures, and do you carry product liability cover?

gaps.what: Retention of paying customers beyond month one; sensor expansion per customer.
gaps.why_it_matters: Paid customers are at most 5 months old; no churn or expansion data.
gaps.ask_founder: Have any of the 6 paying customers added sensors or cancelled subscriptions?
